title: FAA ground stop delays KC Current’s flight to NWSL semifinal against Gotham FC
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of sports and college teams affected by FAA nationwide ground stop.

The Federal Aviation Administration’s ground stop Friday affected the travel of the Kansas City Current, who were scheduled to fly to New York City for their National Women’s Soccer League semifinal against Gotham FC on Sunday.

The team planned to fly via charter Friday evening and boarded their plane shortly before the ground stop, according to a source with knowledge of the Current’s travel plans who spoke on the condition of anonymity due to the ongoing nature of the team’s planning. The team deplaned after it became clear the delay was indefinite.

“We are collaborating with key stakeholders, including the NWSL and our charter partner, to identify next steps in order to arrive safely ahead of our match against Gotham FC on Sunday,” a Current spokesperson said.

The Utah Royals, who will face the Washington Spirit in the other semifinal, at noon ET on Saturday, traveled Thursday and were not affected, a Royals spokesperson confirmed to The Athletic.

Amid widespread disruption in U.S. sports, the U.S. men’s national soccer team is scheduled to play Haiti on Saturday in Miami. That match will not be affected, a spokesperson for Concacaf, the regional governing body in charge of the match, told The Athletic, as both teams and the match officials are already Miami.

“Everyone is already on-site, and the match will proceed as scheduled,” the spokesperson said.

U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said in a social media post that FAA technicians are investigating a “communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.”

This is not the first disruption NWSL teams have faced ahead of the league’s penultimate weekend, although the other was unrelated to travel.

After Gotham FC and the Washington Spirit secured hosting rights to the semifinals last weekend, the league and teams had to scramble to secure venues and locations.

The Spirit were able to negotiate with D.C. United and organizers for the Secretaries’ Cup, an annual NCAA Division III college football game between the U.S. Coast Guard Academy and the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy, to play at their usual home venue of Audi Field at noon ET Saturday. The Spirit will play ahead of the football game, which will start at approximately 4:30 p.m. ET. The field will be lined for both sports (NWSL lines in yellow and football yard lines in white) to avoid having to repaint between games. The bases for the field goal posts will also be in place and padded during the NWSL match.

In New Jersey, Gotham had to move their home game from Sports Illustrated Stadium to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island in New York due to poor pitch conditions at their usual home stadium. That match is scheduled to take place at 3 p.m. ET on Sunday with Gotham providing complimentary transportation services to the 5,000-seat venue for fans in the New York area.
